# Results — Study 338 (Preferred-Stocks) on the real total-return tapes

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One question — is **PFF**
(iShares Preferred & Income Securities ETF) the bond-like-safety-with-an-equity-yield it
is sold as, or equity-grade crash risk wearing a fat coupon? — run on the **total-return**
tapes against **SPY** (equity) and **IEF** (7-10y Treasuries). As-of **2026-05-31** (last
complete month; the partial June 2026 bar is dropped). Match the fingerprint to confirm you
hold the same tapes.*

## Data stamp

PFF lists **2007-03-30**, which bounds the joint window honestly — and means preferreds'
first stress test on this tape was the 2008 crisis.

| Series | Window | Rows | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| **Joint panel (PFF, SPY, IEF, total return)** | 2007-03-30 → 2026-05-29 | 4,822 | `225bc4dab397` |

## The three arms — total return, 2007–2026

| Arm | CAGR | Vol | Sharpe (raw) | Max drawdown |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **PFF (preferreds)** | **3.88%** | **18.7%** | 0.298 | **−65.5%** |
| SPY (equity) | 11.16% | 19.7% | 0.635 | −55.2% |
| IEF (7-10y Treasuries) | 3.26% | 7.0% | 0.495 | −23.9% |

PFF's **return** is bond-like (3.88% CAGR, barely above IEF's 3.26%). PFF's **risk** is
equity-grade or worse: its volatility (18.7%) is within a whisker of stocks', and its worst
drawdown (**−65.5%**) is *deeper than the S&P 500's*. You are paid a bond's return for an
equity's risk. *(Sharpe is raw — there is no part-cash leg here, so all three arms race on
the same footing; label is honest.)*

## Who does PFF actually move with?

| Statistic | Value |
|---|--:|
| Full-sample beta of PFF to **SPY** | **+0.550** (HAC *t* = **+5.58**) |
| Full-sample beta of PFF to **IEF** | −0.206 (HAC *t* = −2.02) |
| **Downside** beta to SPY (worst 10% of SPY days) | **+0.98** |
| **Downside** beta to IEF (worst 10% of SPY days) | +0.10 |
| Correlation PFF/SPY · PFF/IEF | +0.58 · −0.08 |

PFF loads on **equities, not bonds** — and the loading *intensifies in the tail*: on the
worst 10% of equity days its beta to stocks is essentially **1.0**. The equity-comovement
is robust to autocorrelation (HAC *t* = **+5.58**, well clear of 2). → Signal **REAL**: the
equity-like crash risk is statistically real, not noise.

## The decisive test — every >10% equity crash

Did PFF cushion (rise, like a bond) or pile on (fall, like equity)?

| Equity drawdown | SPY | PFF | IEF |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2007-10 → 2009-03 (GFC) | −55.2% | **−63.7%** | +20.2% |
| 2015-07 → 2016-02 | −13.0% | −5.0% | +7.4% |
| 2018-01 → 2018-02 | −10.1% | −2.4% | −1.2% |
| 2018-09 → 2018-12 | −19.3% | −8.1% | +3.4% |
| 2020-02 → 2020-03 (COVID) | −33.7% | −30.8% | +6.4% |
| 2022-01 → 2022-10 | −24.5% | −18.5% | −15.4% |
| 2025-02 → 2025-04 | −18.8% | −7.6% | +2.7% |

**PFF fell in 7 of 7 equity crashes; bonds (IEF) rose in 5 of 7** (the exceptions, 2018-01
and 2022, are the two rate-shock selloffs where bonds also fell — yet PFF fell *with* them).
In the GFC PFF lost
**−63.7%** — *more than the S&P 500* — exactly when its "safety" was supposed to matter,
while Treasuries gained +20%. The preferred-stock "cushion" is the opposite of a cushion.

## How to read it

- **The equity-like crash risk is real.** PFF's beta to equities is +0.55 (HAC *t* 5.58),
  rising to ~1.0 in the tail; it fell in every one of seven equity crashes and lost more
  than stocks in the GFC. → Signal **REAL**.
- **The "bond-like safety" is the mirage.** You collect a coupon worth roughly a Treasury's
  total return (CAGR 3.88% vs 3.26%) while bearing equity-grade volatility and a *deeper*
  drawdown than the S&P 500 — junior, callable, rate-sensitive, illiquid in stress. As a
  *safe* income sleeve it does not survive contact with a crash. → Tradability **MIRAGE**.
- **"Bond-like safety?" → BUSTED.** Senior-to-common and a fixed coupon do not make a
  bond. In the only environment where the distinction matters — the crash — PFF behaved
  like stock, not like a bond.
